summary: A scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Zong Rinpoche studied under Trijang Rinpoche. He held a post at Ganden Shartse Monastery from around 1937 to 1946.

Specializing in philosophy and sinology, Mou studied at Peking University (~1929–1933) and under Shili Xiong (~1930–1950). He held posts at Zhejiang University, National Taiwan University, National Taiwan Normal University, Tunghai University, and as Professor at New Asia Institute (~1974–1995).

Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Gelle studied as a PhD candidate at the University of Vienna (attested 2019). Her posts include Eötvös Loránd University (2014–2016), Budapest Centre for Buddhist Studies (2014–2016), Tibet House Foundation (2002), and East-West Research Institute.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Ito studied at the University of Tokyo (~1965–1970). He served as a professor at Rissho University (~1976–2013) and held posts at the University of Tokyo and Waseda University.

Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Yamaguchi studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1953) and under Rolf Alfred Stein and Jacques Bacot. He held academic posts at Nagoya University and the University of Tokyo (1970–1986).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Nakamura studied at Rissho University (~1937–1940) and under Susumu Yamaguchi (1944). In 1945, he served as Professor of the Department of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University.
A scholar in sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies, Chavannes studied at École Normale Supérieure (~1885–1888). He served as a professor at Collège de France from 1893 to 1918.

Working in sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, Huber studied at the University of Paris, Collège de France, and École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1899–1901). He held a post at École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1902–1914).

A linguist specializing in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies, Benveniste studied at the University of Paris and under Antoine Meillet. He held posts at École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1927–1972) and Collège de France (1937–1972).

Specializing in Indology and linguistics, Burnouf studied at École Normale Supérieure, the French School at Athens, and under Jean-Louis and Eugène Burnouf. He held professorships at the University of Nancy and Faculté des lettres de Nancy (~1854–1867).
Working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology, Senart studied under Theodor Benfey (~1867–1868). He served as President of the Société Asiatique from 1908 to 1928.

Balázs worked in sinology and history/archaeology, studying under Otto Franke in 1923. He held posts at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (1949) and as a professor of Chinese economic history at the University of Paris (~1949–1963).

Lamotte studied Indology and Buddhist studies at KU Leuven, Sapienza, and Paris institutions under Louis de La Vallée Poussin, Sylvain Lévi, and others. He held several posts at KU Leuven (1932–1962) and was President at Université catholique de Louvain (1950–1959).

A scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy, he studied at Wellington College, Magdalene College, and under Pelene Siri Vajirañāṇa. He served in the Royal Artillery (1939–1941) and the Intelligence Corps (1941–1945).

Specializing in religious studies and Indology, Valk studied at Miina Härma Gymnasium and the University of Tartu (~1980–1986). He held a post at the University of Tartu (~1991) and served as an editor for Numen (~2014).
